subject.title: [Bug] PTY silently disabled in sandbox mode without warning when pty:true is set

question: For explicit `pty: true` requests while exec resolves to sandbox mode, should OpenClaw warn and continue without PTY, fail the request, or support PTY inside sandbox backends?
rationale: The current behavior sits on the sandboxed exec boundary; warning-only is the smallest repair, but warning versus error versus backend PTY support is a maintainer product/security choice.

options.title: Warn and keep sandbox non-PTY
options.body: Add a visible warning when explicit PTY is ignored in sandbox mode, preserve current sandbox execution behavior, and document the limitation.

options.title: Fail explicit sandbox PTY
options.body: Return an invalid-request style error when sandbox mode cannot honor an explicit PTY request, avoiding a downgraded run.

options.title: Support sandbox PTY
options.body: Allow sandbox backends to allocate PTY where safe, which is broader and needs backend-specific security and runtime proof.

recommendation.title: Warn and keep sandbox non-PTY
recommendation.body: Add a visible warning when explicit PTY is ignored in sandbox mode, preserve current sandbox execution behavior, and document the limitation.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history points to this owner for the original PTY support and the central exec approval path.
